primitives.name: Margin of Victory Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: y ~ Normal(a_rank[p1] - a_rank[p2] + h·b, σ_y), where abilities a_j depend only on world-ranking slot j (not the player), b ∈ {-1,0,1} encodes home advantage, h is the home effect.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y': 'margin of victory in games (dimensionless, values -3..-1, 1..3)', 'a_rank': 'player ability parameter indexed by ranking slot (unitless)', 'h': 'home advantage magnitude (unitless)', 'b': 'home indicator variable ∈ {-1, 0, 1}', 'σ_y': 'outcome noise scale (unitless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Outcome margin is normally distributed around ability difference plus home effect; abilities depend only on ranking slot.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ranking slots are not informative or when player-specific variation dominates.

primitives.name: Rank-Based Ability Prior
primitives.verbatim_quote: Hierarchical prior on abilities: a_j ~ Normal(β(j-1) + γ√(j-1), σ_a) — linear + square-root rank trend capturing diminishing ability gaps at worse ranks.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'α_j': 'ability of rank-j player (unitless)', 'β': 'linear rank coefficient (unitless)', 'γ': 'square-root rank coefficient (unitless)', 'σ_a': 'scale of ability variation (unitless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player abilities follow a trend that diminishes with lower ranks; shrinkage toward mean ability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At very high or low ranks, where sample sizes are small or extreme performance occurs.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to derive player strength profiles from tournament data without overfitting to individual matches.
layer2.telemetry: Ability posterior means and credible intervals per rank

primitives.name: Country-Specific Home Intercept
primitives.verbatim_quote: Second model adds country-specific home intercepts (Egypt, England, USA) on top of a global h.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'h_global': 'global home advantage (unitless)', 'h_country': 'country-specific home adjustment (unitless)', 'b_country': 'country indicator variable (unitless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Home advantage varies systematically by host country due to venue, crowd, or cultural factors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When host country has insufficient match history or when cultural bias is negligible.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that home advantage in squash can be quantified through a Bayesian hierarchical model where match outcomes are modeled as normally-distributed margins of victory. The model uses rank-based ability priors to avoid overfitting to sparse data, and introduces country-specific intercepts to capture heterogeneous home effects. This structure allows for principled uncertainty quantification and generalization across tournaments. The failure mode arises when the normality assumption breaks down or when player-specific deviations are not adequately captured by ranking alone. The model assumes that margin of victory contains more information than binary win/loss, which is validated empirically via posterior predictive checks. The use of Stan enables robust MCMC inference, ensuring reliable estimates even under complex hierarchical structures.
